paraphrase: Yoni mudrā: in siddhāsana, closing the ears, eyes, nostrils and mouth with the thumbs, index, middle, ring and other fingers, drawing in prāṇa by kākī (mudrā) and joining it with apāna, contemplating the six centres in order with the mantra 'huṃ haṃsa', one brings consciousness to the sleeping serpent-goddess, raises the power with the jīva to the supreme lotus, becomes full of power and contemplates union with Śiva and supreme bliss — 'I am Brahman'. This yoni mudrā is most secret, hard even for the gods; one established in it even once is in samādhi; by its practice even the slayer of a brahmin, of an embryo, the drinker of liquor and the violator of the guru's bed is not stained, and all terrible sins and lesser sins perish.

paraphrase: Making śāmbhavī mudrā one brings about the perception of the self; seeing the bindu made of Brahman one fixes the mind there; put the self in space and space in the self; seeing the self as made of space one is not hindered by anything and, full of bliss, abides in samādhi.

paraphrase: When by the practice of khecarī the tongue goes upward, success in samādhi comes, leaving ordinary activity. Performing the bhrāmarī retention with slow breath and exhaling very slowly, the sound of a bee arises; hearing the bee-sound within one leads the mind there; samādhi arises there, and bliss: 'I am He' (so'ham).
